title: Transport of product normalization through completed realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, $a\ge1$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$ and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the specified exchange, projection and completed-operation data [def-exchange-projection, fix-lem-exchanges]. Let $f=aj:X\to B$, $g=bk:Y\to B$, and optionally $h=dl:W\to B$ be compactifications of separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes; put $T=X\times_BY$, $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $u=j\times_Bk$, $c:\bar T\to B$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Take integral $D^b_{ctf}$ inputs $K,L,M$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and their actual strict reduction systems. Assume every intermediate system in the product words has normalized reductions, compatible etale origins and common bounded cohomological and Tor intervals, so the specified comparisons
$$c_V:\mathcal L V(\mathcal RK,\mathcal RL,\mathcal RM)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{\mathrm{int}}(K,L,M)$$
of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] apply, with $\mathcal L=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$.
Suppose $e_\bullet:(J_jK_\bullet)\boxtimes(J_kL_\bullet)\cong J_u(K_\bullet\boxtimes L_\bullet)$ is the ordered word in normalized open base-change and tensor generators, that its signed-symmetry and triple-associativity equations hold in the whole derived system category, and that the specified exchange/projection words satisfy $\lambda^{\mathscr S}_{aj,bk}=S_c(e_\bullet)\lambda^{\mathscr S}_{a,b}$. Here $\lambda$ is the ordered composite explicitly defined in [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity], applied to the system operations; the assumptions concern actual system morphisms, not levelwise equalities.
Then $e^c=c_{J_u(-)}\mathcal L(e_\bullet)c_{(-)\boxtimes(-)}^{-1}$ is the canonical natural completed open external-tensor isomorphism, restricts to the identity, and satisfies those same signed-symmetry and triple-associativity equations with the actual completed associators. After termwise restriction of scalars from semilinear systems to constant-$R$ towers, the normalized system proper/open generator in these words is exactly the tower map $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison], with its canonical finite evaluation on each bounded etale-origin input; its completed counterpart is the total-limit realization of that map under the specified $c_V$ comparisons. For every ordered exchange/projection word $m:S\to V$ in this calculation one has
$$c_V\mathcal L(m)=m_{\mathrm{int}}c_S.$$
In particular its completed compactification identity is $\lambda_{aj,bk}=Rc_*(e^c)\lambda_{a,b}$ as an equality of the specified maps.
Under the rationalization and scalar-extension comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction, def-exchange-projection], the images of these maps are exactly the prescribed maps with $E$ coefficients and, over a common finite coefficient field, with $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ coefficients. All these equations persist and are independent of enlarging that common field, with its stipulated scalar-extension composition cocycle. This is a transport implication from system equations; it does not assert them from finite evaluations and assumes no faithfulness of finite reduction on integral derived morphisms.

proof.text: Use the realization isomorphisms of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] with the parentheses of each expression retained. Their hypotheses hold for every intermediate by assumption: the systems are normalized, have compatible etale origins, and have common finite cohomological and Tor bounds. That theorem intertwines the system open maps, units, counits, tensor/pullback constraints, direct-image compositors and proper/open interchange with the specified integral maps, including every outer expression context. Thus for each generator $a:S\to V$, also when whiskered, we have $c_V\mathcal L(a)=a_{\rm int}c_S$. Expand the exchange and projection generators by the unit--square--counit and open/proper composites of [def-exchange-projection]; these use exactly the generators just listed, with the specified compactification identifications. This invokes an actual transformation comparison, not a comparison only of endpoint objects. The tensor reassociation and the Koszul-signed symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ are generators as well. For normalized systems $M,N,H$ (here the systems $M_V$), [lem-pur-normalized-tensor-constraint-transport] gives the whole-system coefficient square $\gamma_Q\mathcal R(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P$ for the system constraint $a$ and the actual completed constraint $\widehat a$. Its primitive tensor comparison is the defining quotient-model comparison followed by $\mathcal L(e\otimes e)$, which is the inverse of the map $a_\otimes$ entering $c_{V\otimes T}$, so $\gamma$ is the realization's $r$. Hence [lem-sf-expression-contextual-intertwining] gives $c\,\mathcal L(a)=\widehat a\,c$ for these constraints in every outer context.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: tensor reassociation, evaluation and adjunction units and counits; agent application of the existing realization theorem on the assumed domain

proof.text:
Here and below composition is written right to left. The generator equation extends to any ordered word by the following explicit cancellation. The empty word has $c_S\mathcal L(1_S)=c_S$. If $a:S\to V$ and $b:V\to W$ have the equation, then
$$c_W\mathcal L(ba)=b_{\rm int}c_V\mathcal L(a)=b_{\rm int}a_{\rm int}c_S.$$
If $a$ is invertible, its equation gives
$$c_S\mathcal L(a^{-1})=a_{\rm int}^{-1}c_V.$$
The contextual generator equations in step 1 already cover unary whiskering and tensoring in either slot; a simultaneous change of both tensor slots is the composite of those two changes by the bifunctor law. Induction on the finite list of contextual generators therefore gives $c_V\mathcal L(m)=m_{\rm int}c_S$ for every word in question, with no change of parentheses.

source.place: Inherited-equations sentence; explicit functoriality and cancellation for finite ordered words

proof.text: Apply step 2 to the assumed normalized open-base-change/tensor word $e_\bullet$. Its transported word is exactly the ordered word of canonical completed open maps: the realization theorem identifies these with the localized completed-ring maps. Hence it is the canonical completed open external-tensor comparison, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism with the same endpoints, and it is $e^c=c_{J_u(-)}\mathcal L(e_\bullet)c_{(-)\boxtimes(-)}^{-1}$. Its inverse is $c_{(-)\boxtimes(-)}\mathcal L(e_\bullet^{-1})c_{J_u(-)}^{-1}$, as multiplication cancels both middle comparison pairs; naturality follows by substituting the naturality equations for the three factors. For the restriction normalization, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] says that each system open base-change or tensor generator restricts to the identity under its open units. Composing these identities gives the identity on $K_\bullet\boxtimes L_\bullet$. The realization theorem intertwines these units, restriction and tensor comparisons, so the same word after completed restriction is $c_D\mathcal L(1_D)c_D^{-1}=1$, where $D$ is the restricted product expression. This proves the asserted restriction identity.

source.place: Proper-reduction sentence: normalized open external-tensor identification; agent transport of the assumed system word

proof.text: Let $P,Q:A\to B$ be the two paths in either of the assumed signed-symmetry and triple-associativity diagrams, retaining every swap, associator, pullback compositor and open-extension compositor as a letter. Step 2 identifies their completed paths with $c_B\mathcal L(P)c_A^{-1}$ and $c_B\mathcal L(Q)c_A^{-1}$. Since $P=Q$ in the whole derived system category, applying the functor $\mathcal L$ gives equality of these two paths. By step 1 the swap and associator letters are carried to the actual completed signed symmetry and associator, and the composition and open letters to the actual completed maps, by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]; no constraint is defined anew by this equation. Thus the resulting equalities have the prescribed Koszul symmetry and completed associators. No equality is inferred by evaluating at a finite level.

source.place: Symmetry and associativity assertions in the coherence proof; elementary conjugation of the system equations assumed in the item

proof.text: For a proper/open square $Q$, the realization theorem identifies restriction of the semilinear-system generator to constant-$R$ towers with the normalized constant-tower mate $\gamma_Q$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Apply [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] to the constant system $C_n=R$ with $B=R$, where restriction is the identity: this mate is the $J_i\dashv G_i$ adjunct of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$ for the tower isomorphism $\lambda_Q$ built by restricting $p$ to $V\times_ZW$, factoring $k$ through the clopen lift and composing direct images. That is exactly the $\lambda_Q$ of [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison], whose $\Gamma_Q$ is defined as the same adjunct. The adjunction bijection therefore identifies the actual tower morphisms, all within the constant-$R$ tower category. This is the asserted $\Gamma_Q$. Its canonical finite evaluation is exactly the one in the tower-comparison statement, applied to the supplied bounded etale-origin reductions with their scalar-restriction identifications. The finite-type field-base and finite coefficient hypotheses are already those of the realization domain. Finally the realization theorem's proper/open generator equation gives $c_{S_pJ_k}\mathcal L(\Gamma_Q)=\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}c_{J_iS_r}$, where on the left $\mathcal L$ includes restriction of scalars. Thus the completed generator is the total-limit realization of the tower arrow. The tower arrow itself and the completed arrow are in different categories; their equality is asserted only through this displayed comparison.

source.place: Proper/open generator normalization; Stacks 0F7B lemma-shriek-proper-and-open and 0F7F lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change underpin the cited tower theorem

proof.text:
Write $A$ for the source expression of the system product map, $B$ for the proper compactified product target, and $C$ for the target after open extension. By [lem-sf-product-compactification-identity] the symbol $\lambda$ means the explicitly ordered word $\alpha\circ S_g(\operatorname{PF}_q\circ(\operatorname{Ex}\otimes1))\circ\Psi_g$, with $\Psi_g$ the two-symmetry/projection word. We use that definition, not that node's finite-coefficient identity as an integral assertion. Step 2 identifies these words with the specified completed words. Applying $\mathcal L$ to the system identity assumed in the item gives
$$\lambda_{aj,bk}=c_C\mathcal L(S_c(e_\bullet))\mathcal L(\lambda^{\mathscr S}_{a,b})c_A^{-1}
=(c_C\mathcal L(S_c(e_\bullet))c_B^{-1})(c_B\mathcal L(\lambda^{\mathscr S}_{a,b})c_A^{-1})
=Rc_*(e^c)\lambda_{a,b}.$$
The last equality uses the realization theorem's natural direct-image comparison, including outer contexts, for the first factor, and step 2 for the second. This is equality of the prescribed completed maps.

source.place: Proper-reduction sentence: product compactification identity, transported from the assumed whole-system equality

proof.text: For rationalization, apply the coefficient functor to every equality just proved. [lem-fix-operation-reduction] intertwines the operations and preserves tensor associativity, evaluations, units and counits. [def-exchange-projection] specifies the rational maps as rationalizations of the integral maps and the scalar-extension comparisons as intertwining their defining constituents. Therefore each contextual generator is the prescribed field-coefficient generator; for a composite, the coefficient isomorphism at each intermediate vertex cancels with its inverse exactly as in step 2. The images of $e^c$, $\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}$, and the two $\lambda$ words are consequently the specified rational maps, with all displayed equations. For algebraically closed coefficients choose a common finite coefficient field for all data and apply the same argument there. The rational symmetry and associator are the rationalizations of the integral ones, and under completed scalar extension the system constraints of [lem-pur-normalized-tensor-constraint-transport] commute with the canonical scalar tensor comparison, scalars having degree zero, so the same limit argument as in step 1 carries them to the common-stage constraints. If $E\subset F\subset H$, the stipulated composition cocycle identifies direct transport to $H$ with the transport through $F$; substituting it on the two endpoints of each arrow cancels the intermediate comparisons. The two arrows hence represent the same common-stage morphism, independently of enlargement. This uses only the supplied coefficient domains and cocycle, and never reduces a rational object modulo $t^n$.

Clarified the category of the tower Gamma arrow versus its completed realization. Reused existing nodes; created no nodes. tool_uses.why: Generic realization theorem for finite operation expressions and their contextual generators, on exactly the normalized bounded etale-origin domain assumed here; it supplies the coefficient comparison tool, not a replacement Kunneth proof.
Canonical open-unit normalization of base-change and tensor maps, including ringed diagram sites, supplies restriction identities for the specified e word.
Identifies the constant-R tower arrow by its open-adjunction transpose and states its actual finite evaluation; used solely to recognize the normalized generator.
Generic operation and structural-map compatibility with rationalization and scalar extension, used to carry the established integral equations to field coefficients.

Generic whole-system/completed identification of the tensor reassociation and Koszul-signed symmetry; the realization theorem's generator list omits the symmetry, which the swap letters of the product words and of Psi need.
Generic conversion of a whole-system coefficient square into the realization equation c L(tau)=tau_int c in every outer context, applied to the tensor-constraint generators.

Its constant-system case identifies the normalized constant-tower proper/open mate with the open adjunct of the inverse clopen restriction, so that the restricted system generator is the Gamma_Q of the tower comparison.
